title: Interchangeable biological product substitution
rule_summary: A Massachusetts pharmacist may substitute a biological product for a prescribed brand-name biological product under M.G.L. c.112, §12EE only when FDA has determined the substitute is interchangeable with the prescribed product and the prescriber has not prohibited substitution for that patient. The statute also requires patient notification, prescriber communication after substitution, and record retention.
exam_relevance: Tests the legal distinction between a biosimilar and an FDA-designated interchangeable biological product.
common_confusions: Biosimilar status alone is not the statutory substitution trigger; the product must be FDA-determined interchangeable.
verification_notes: Current official Massachusetts authority verified during Pre-Batch3 T2 authoring on 2026-08-18; fresh independent legal and realism audit is still required before release.
